entries.note: A game action's availability is the referenced record's preflight, injected rather than recomputed: the host passes games.inspect and the replaceable worker passes a call to the retained host's game-config route, so the verdict a dashboard row shows is the same one the launch will apply and there is no second copy of the executable/requires/cwd/surface checks to drift. A thrown preflight (an unknown gameId is a 404) becomes the row's own issue instead of failing the whole listing, and a workspace layer that cannot preflight at all says so rather than rendering the action as available.

entries.note:
Availability is computed by resolving each required file through the root boundary (a symlink escaping the root counts as missing) and by an explicit PATH walk with the same shell environment terminals get (PATHEXT on Windows). A declaration or dashboard error is returned with empty groups instead of thrown so the tab can render it while formats keep working.

CORRECTED by contract 4 (spec 081): the old claim that "nothing is executed and nothing is cached" no longer holds, and the id is now a historical name rather than a description. An action bound to a device runs that device's declared probe, and probe results ARE cached for 15 s with in-flight coalescing (devices.mjs). Nothing else is executed: the action's own command is still never run to decide availability. The freshly-copied-pcvr-host.env property survives, because requires/tools are still stat/PATH checks with no cache of their own — but a device that comes back up can be up to 15 s stale here, and the Devices section's refresh is the explicit way to bypass that.

entries.note: Every action is evaluated against its device, not only the ones that look remote, because the device defaults to local and an unbound action must still report which device it ran its checks against. The probe cost is bounded by the cache and its in-flight coalescing in devices.mjs: this map runs under Promise.all, so a plain TTL would let every action miss at once. The action's own requires/tools are checked first and both halves are pushed, so the reported reason names what actually has to change. A game action still short-circuits to its record's preflight only when nothing else is missing, so one message is reported rather than a pile.

Running goes through the retained host's terminal route with a payload built here (bash + resolved script + literal args + env for scripts, the argv itself for logs) so the replaceable worker never spawns PTYs; unavailable actions are refused with the missing items and capture actions are redirected. Captures reuse the format runner (no shell, cwd = root, 10 s / 8 MiB), require the PNG signature before touching disk, create `into` after a lexical boundary check and confine its realpath, then write the image and the manifest through temp-and-rename; a same-millisecond collision gets a numeric suffix. The returned title also overrides the snapshot because a retained host older than the title option labels sessions generically. The action is now selected once by dashboardAction and passed in, because a game action does not produce a terminal payload at all: the caller launches it through the project game route and returns that game session, so this function refuses the game kind the way it already refuses capture.
